fps_detail_disabled: FPS is disabled. Tick “FPS (foreground app)” in the metrics list above to enable capture and show it in the overlay.
fps_detail_requires_elevation: Starting an ETW capture session requires administrator rights or membership in the Performance Log Users group. HardwareOSD never elevates itself silently — use the button below.
fps_detail_no_foreground: No foreground window. Switch to a game or graphics application to measure its frame rate.
fps_detail_no_frames: The foreground application is not presenting frames through DXGI/D3D9 (or has just started).
fps_detail_displayed_unavailable: Displayed FPS needs DWM present correlation, which this backend does not implement. Choose Automatic or Presented.
fps_detail_short: ETW present timing. FPS·p marks presented fallback data.
fps_detail_capturing: Presented frame timing measured from ETW present events.
fps_detail_capturing_fallback: Presented timing (displayed timing unavailable); the overlay marks it FPS·p.
fps_detail_holding: No new present events arrived; the last valid FPS is held briefly, then --.
fps_detail_no_game: The foreground window is not a fullscreen game. Game Only measures fullscreen games to avoid showing desktop UI frame rates; enable “Measure windowed apps” if needed.
fps_measure_windowed_hint: Also measure windowed applications. Desktop UI, Steam, browsers and Electron shells can then be reported as FPS, so leave this off for games.
fps_permission_needed: FPS capture needs one-time permission. Windows will ask for administrator approval to add this account to Performance Log Users. No password is stored and no background administrator task is created.
fps_permission_relogon: Permission granted. Sign out and back in to activate it. For this session only, you can restart elevated.
fps_permission_granted: FPS permission granted. Sign out and back in to activate it.
fps_permission_helper_missing: The elevated permission helper is unavailable.
fps_detail_busiest: The foreground process is not presenting through DXGI/D3D9; showing the busiest presenting process ({0}).
fps_capture_mode_hint: Game Only measures fullscreen or borderless games. All Applications also measures windowed games, Steam, browsers and other apps that present through DXGI/D3D9.
fps_detail_no_presenter: The foreground application does not present frames through DXGI/D3D9. Classic GDI/WPF apps and the Windows desktop are composed by DWM and are not measured in this mode.
fps_detail_desktop: The Windows desktop is composed by DWM; application FPS is undefined. Switch to an app that presents frames.
fps_detail_focus_grace: Foreground changed; holding the last valid FPS briefly.
fps_detail_ambiguous: Several related processes are presenting; the target is ambiguous, so no value is shown.
fps_measure_windowed_all_apps: All Applications already includes windowed apps.
metrics_page_subtitle: Choose what the OSD displays and where each reading comes from.
metrics_hint: Order controls the left-to-right position inside each row. Move a metric up or down to reorder it. Source shows where each reading comes from; N/A means the hardware or interface does not expose it.
metrics_how_1: FPS is measured from real-time ETW frame-presentation events (Microsoft-Windows-DXGI and Microsoft-Windows-D3D9), the same documented interfaces PresentMon builds on. The foreground window's process is identified with GetForegroundWindow, then only that process's present timestamps are used. No DLL is injected, no game memory is read and no input is intercepted.
metrics_how_2: Starting an ETW session requires administrator rights; HardwareOSD never elevates itself silently. Without elevation the FPS row shows -- and the Metrics page explains why. Values marked FPS·p are presented-frame timing: displayed-frame timing needs DWM correlation and is not provided by the current backend.
metrics_how_3: Games that render through DXGI (D3D11/D3D12) or D3D9 are supported. Vulkan/OpenGL titles that bypass these providers show -- rather than an estimated value.

general_about_text:
HardwareOSD {0} · .NET {1} · x64
Sensor interfaces: NVIDIA NVML, LibreHardwareMonitor (MPL-2.0), Windows PDH, NtQuerySystemInformation, GlobalMemoryStatusEx, ETW present events.
No game injection, no game memory access, no input hooks, no anti-cheat interaction.

recording_page_subtitle: Log sensor readings from the live cache to CSV or TXT.
recording_config_hint: The recorder samples the latest published snapshot; it never starts a second hardware poll.
recording_file_hint: The extension follows the selected format. Existing files are never overwritten.
recording_sensors_hint: Only sensors present in the live cache are listed. Unavailable readings are written as blanks, not zeros.
recording_refresh_hint: The list refreshes when the page is opened or the language changes.
recording_about_1: CSV uses one row per sensor value with an explicit Status and Note column.
recording_about_2: A background writer drains a bounded queue; a slow disk drops samples instead of growing memory.
recording_about_3: SensorCache is read-only. Unavailable values stay blank and the reason is kept in the Note column.
